You're not the only one. That is literally the whole debate that splits the Ballad fandom in half.

The Snow-defender side is exactly what you said: He was a Capitol golden boy, he lost everything, he got sent to District 12 as a Peacekeeper, he got exiled, he risked getting hanged, all to run away with her. And then she leaves him in the woods because he killed Mayfair, who was literally about to turn them both in and get them killed.

From that angle, yeah, it looks like she did him dirty.

But the Lucy Gray side is that Snow didn't throw everything away for her. He threw everything away for himself, and she was just the excuse he used to feel like a good person while he did it.

Look at the order of what he actually did:

He didn't get exiled because of Lucy Gray. He got exiled because he cheated to help her win, and then got caught. He betrayed Sejanus, his best friend, to save his own skin. Sejanus gets hanged because Snow snitched on him.

He didn't kill Mayfair just to protect Lucy Gray. He killed Mayfair because Mayfair saw them together in the woods with Sejanus's guns, and if Mayfair talked, Snow was dead. It was self-preservation. Same with Billy Taupe. Snow didn't kill Billy to protect Lucy, Mayfair did. Snow just cleaned it up.

And the moment that actually breaks Lucy Gray isn't just one killing. It's that she watches him kill and feel nothing. No guilt, no panic, no "oh god what did I do." He just calmly covers it up, lies about it, and starts planning his next move.

That's when she realizes what we as readers already know: Snow doesn't love people, he collects people. He loved the idea of Lucy Gray being his, of her singing for him, of him being the hero who saved her. But the second she became a liability, he was ready to shoot her in the woods too. And he tries to. He literally unloads a gun at her voice in the trees.

So she didn't turn on him for killing one guy. She turned on him because she finally saw the pattern:

He kills Bobbin and calls it strategy.
He gets Sejanus killed and calls it loyalty.
He kills Mayfair and calls it protection.
He tries to kill her and calls it love.

Lucy Gray didn't betray Snow. She survived him. She was the only person who ever saw who he was before he became President Snow, and she got out while she still could.

That's why it's so tragic. Snow thinks she betrayed him, so he spends the next 65 years hating District 12, hating mockingjays, hating the song she sang. But she didn't betray him. She just refused to be his next victim.

So you're not wrong for feeling bad for him in that scene. Collins wrote him to be sympathetic in that moment on purpose. But the reason he ends up alone in that woods screaming her name isn't because she left him. It's because she finally understood him.
